text: Daraz Knowledge Base Complaint Escalation Process Document Code: CS-002 | Version: 1.3 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. When to Escalate ● The customer's issue was not resolved after the standard support flow. ● The case involves a payment dispute, suspected fraud, or safety concern. ● The customer explicitly requests escalation to a supervisor. ● The same issue has recurred multiple times for the same order. 2. Escalation Levels Level Handled By Typical SLA Level 1 Frontline support agent First response per channel SLA Level 2 Team lead / specialist queue 1–2 business days Level 3 Trust & Safety / Policy team 3–5 business days Level 4 Management review (rare, high-impact cases) 5–10 business days 3. Documentation Requirements Every escalation must include the order ID, a summary of prior contact attempts, evidence provided by the customer, and the specific resolution being requested, to avoid asking the customer to repeat information. 4. Resolution Authority ● Level 1–2 agents: standard refunds/replacements within policy limits. ● Level 3: policy exceptions, seller penalty decisions, goodwill gestures beyond standard limits. ● Level 4: account-level actions such as permanent seller suspension or legal referral. 5. Customer Follow-Up Once an escalated case is resolved, the customer must be notified of the outcome and reasoning. If a case is closed without the customer's requested resolution, the notification must explain why and note any further appeal options.

Daraz Knowledge Base Customer Support Guidelines Document Code: CS-001 | Version: 1.8 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. Support Channels ● In-app / website live chat. ● Help center with self-service FAQs and order-specific help flows. ● Phone support for priority or unresolved issues. ● Social media channels for general inquiries (not for sharing personal or payment details). 2. Response Time Targets Channel Target First Response Target Resolution Live Chat < 5 minutes Same session where possible Help Center Ticket < 24 hours 2–5 business days Phone Support Immediate (queue dependent) Same call where possible Social Media < 12 hours Redirected to ticket if complex 3. Information Needed From Customers ● Order ID or tracking number. ● Description of the issue and, where relevant, photos or video. ● Preferred resolution (refund, replacement, exchange, information). 4. Tiered Support Model Tier 1 agents handle common queries (order status, general policy questions, basic returns). Complex cases — payment disputes, suspected fraud, repeated seller violations — are escalated to Tier 2 specialist teams or Trust & Safety. 5. Customer Communication Standards ● Use clear, respectful, and jargon-free language. ● Never request full card numbers, passwords, or OTPs over chat or phone. ● Confirm resolution details in writing (chat transcript or email) for the customer's records.

Daraz Knowledge Base Delivery & Shipping Policy Document Code: DEL-001 | Version: 3.1 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. Purpose This policy outlines shipping methods, delivery timelines, fees, and customer responsibilities for receiving orders placed on the platform. 2. Delivery Options ● Standard Delivery — the default option for most orders. ● Express Delivery — available for select items and locations at an added fee. ● Scheduled Delivery — customer selects a preferred delivery date/time window. ● Store/Locker Pickup — customer collects the order from a designated point. Zone Standard Delivery Express Delivery Major City (Metro) 2–4 business days Next-day, where available Secondary City 3–6 business days 1–2 business days Remote / Rural Area 5–9 business days Not typically available Cross-border Import 7–15 business days Not available 3. Shipping Fees Shipping fees are calculated based on item weight, dimensions, delivery zone, and any active free-shipping promotions or minimum-order thresholds. The exact fee is always shown at checkout before payment confirmation. 4. Failed Delivery Attempts Couriers will typically attempt delivery up to three times. If delivery cannot be completed, the customer is notified and the parcel may be held at a local hub for pickup or returned to the seller, in which case a refund is issued minus any applicable shipping fee. 5. Tracking A tracking number is generated once the seller hands the parcel to the courier. Customers can track status in real time from the "My Orders" page or via the courier's own tracking portal. 6. Customer Responsibilities ● Provide an accurate, complete delivery address and a reachable phone number. ● Be available at the delivery address during the estimated delivery window. ● Inspect the package for visible damage before accepting delivery where possible.

Daraz Knowledge Base Delivery Timelines by Region Document Code: DEL-002 | Version: 2.0 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. Order Processing Time Sellers are required to hand over ready-to-ship orders to the courier partner within 24–48 hours of order confirmation, unless the listing specifies a longer processing/production time (e.g., custom or pre-order items). 2. Estimated Delivery Time (EDT) Calculation EDT shown at checkout = seller processing time + courier transit time for the destination zone + any buffer for public holidays or weather disruptions. Order Type Typical Processing Time In-stock, local seller 1 business day In-stock, cross-border seller 2–3 business days Pre-order As stated on listing (can exceed 15 days) Made-to-order / customized 3–10 business days 3. Public Holidays and Peak Campaigns During major sale campaigns (e.g., mega sale days) and public holidays, delivery timelines may extend beyond the standard estimate due to higher parcel volumes. Any such extension is communicated via banner notices on the app and website. 4. Delayed Shipment Compensation ● Customers may request order cancellation with full refund if a shipment has not been dispatched within the promised processing window. ● Repeated late dispatch by a seller may result in a reduced seller performance score and visibility penalties (see Seller Code of Conduct).

Daraz Knowledge Base Cash on Delivery (COD) Policy Document Code: PAY-002 | Version: 1.5 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. What Is Cash on Delivery Cash on Delivery (COD) allows customers to pay in cash at the time the order is physically delivered, rather than paying online in advance. 2. COD Eligibility ● Available only for select categories and order value thresholds. ● May be restricted in remote areas with limited courier cash-handling. ● Not available for digital goods, vouchers, or certain high-value items. ● New accounts or accounts with a history of refused COD orders may have COD temporarily disabled. 3. Customer Responsibilities for COD Orders ● Have the exact or close amount ready at the time of delivery. ● Be reachable at the delivery address during the delivery window. ● Inspect the parcel before payment where the courier allows it. 4. Refused COD Deliveries Orders refused at the doorstep without a valid reason (such as visible tampering) are treated as a failed delivery. Repeated unjustified refusals may lead to COD being disabled on that account, requiring prepaid methods for future orders. 5. COD Refunds Since no online payment was made, COD refunds (for later returns) are issued via bank transfer or e-wallet credit rather than reversal to a card, as described in the Refund Policy.

Daraz Knowledge Base Payment Methods Policy Document Code: PAY-001 | Version: 2.0 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. Accepted Payment Methods ● Credit and debit cards (Visa, Mastercard, and other supported networks). ● Bank transfer / online banking. ● Digital wallets and mobile payment apps. ● Cash on Delivery (COD), where available. ● Buy Now, Pay Later / installment plans, where available. ● Store credit, vouchers, and gift cards. 2. Payment Security Card and bank details are processed through PCI-DSS compliant payment gateways. The platform does not store full card numbers on its own servers; tokenized references are used for recurring or saved-card checkout. 3. Failed or Pending Payments If a payment fails after the amount is deducted from a customer's account, the amount is automatically reversed by the payment provider, typically within 5–7 business days, and the order is not confirmed until payment is verified as successful. 4. Currency and Pricing Prices are displayed in the local currency of the storefront. Cross-border purchases may be subject to currency conversion by the card issuer or payment provider, along with applicable customs or import charges. 5. Installment / Buy Now Pay Later Terms Where offered, installment plans are provided by a third-party finance partner. Approval, interest, and late-payment terms are governed by that partner's own terms and conditions, disclosed at checkout.

Daraz Knowledge Base Refund Methods & Timelines Document Code: REF-002 | Version: 1.4 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. Refund Processing Stages ● Stage 1 — Validation: the return/cancellation reason and any required photo evidence are reviewed. ● Stage 2 — Approval: refund amount is calculated, including any deductions. ● Stage 3 — Disbursement: funds are released to the refund destination chosen by the customer or determined by the original payment method. 2. Refund Amount Calculation Refund amount = item price paid − non-refundable fees (if any) + shipping fee refund (only when the return reason is attributable to the seller or platform, such as damaged or wrong item). Scenario Item Refunded Shipping Fee Refunded Seller sent wrong/damaged item Yes Yes Customer changed mind Yes No Order cancelled pre-dispatch Yes (full) N/A — not charged yet Failed delivery, returned to sender Yes No 3. Store Credit Option Customers may opt to receive a refund as store credit instead of a cash/original-method refund. Store credit is typically issued instantly and may carry a small bonus incentive as disclosed at the time of choice. 4. International / Cross-Border Orders Refunds for cross-border orders may take longer due to additional currency conversion and customs-related processing, typically adding 3–5 extra business days to the standard timeline.

Daraz Knowledge Base Refund Policy Document Code: REF-001 | Version: 2.5 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. When a Refund Applies ● An approved return has passed quality check. ● An order is cancelled before dispatch. ● A delivery attempt fails permanently and the parcel is returned to sender. ● A payment was made but the order could not be fulfilled (out of stock, seller cancellation). ● A price adjustment or goodwill credit is approved by customer support. 2. Refund Methods Refunds are issued to the original payment method by default. For cash-on-delivery (COD) orders, refunds are issued to the customer's e-wallet or bank account, since no card or account was originally charged. Original Payment Method Refund Destination Typical Timeline Credit/Debit Card Same card 5–10 business days Digital Wallet Same wallet 1–3 business days Bank Transfer Same bank account 3–7 business days Cash on Delivery (COD) Platform wallet or bank transfer 3–7 business days Store Credit / Voucher Store credit reissued Instant to 24 hours 3. Partial Refunds Partial refunds may be issued when only part of a multi-item order is returned or cancelled, or when a minor, mutually agreed deduction applies (for example, a missing free gift that cannot be returned separately). 4. Refund Status Tracking Customers can track refund status under "My Orders > Refund Status." Status moves through: Refund Approved → Refund Processing → Refund Completed. Bank processing times beyond the platform's control may add a few extra business days. 5. Failed or Delayed Refunds If a refund does not reflect within the stated timeline, customers should contact Customer Support with the order ID and payment reference. Support will investigate with the payment provider or bank before reprocessing.

Daraz Knowledge Base Return Eligibility & Conditions Document Code: RET-002 | Version: 1.6 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. General Eligibility Conditions ● The return request is raised within the applicable return window for the category. ● The item is unused, unworn, and unwashed, with original tags and packaging intact. ● All original accessories, manuals, freebies, and warranty cards are included. ● The product is not on the non-returnable list for its category. 2. Reasons That Qualify for Free Return Pickup ● Wrong item delivered (different from what was ordered). ● Item received is damaged or defective. ● Item is missing parts or accessories listed on the product page. ● Significant difference between the product description and the item received. ● Counterfeit or non-genuine product suspected. 3. Reasons That May Incur a Return Shipping Fee ● Customer changed their mind ("no longer needed"). ● Wrong size or color ordered by the customer where accurate sizing information was provided. ● Item does not match personal preference or expectation, despite matching the listing. 4. Exchange vs. Return Where stock is available, customers may choose a direct exchange (e.g., for a different size) instead of a refund. Exchanges follow the same eligibility conditions as returns and are subject to one exchange per order line. 5. Proof Requirements For damaged, defective, or incorrect items, customers must upload photos or a short video of the item and its packaging within 48 hours of delivery to qualify for an expedited, fee-free return. 6. Disputes If a seller disputes the reason for return, the case is escalated to the platform's Trust & Safety team, whose decision on eligibility is final for marketplace transactions.

Daraz Knowledge Base Return Policy Document Code: RET-001 | Version: 2.3 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. Purpose This policy defines the conditions under which customers may return items purchased on the platform, the eligible return window, and the process sellers and customers must follow. 2. Standard Return Window Most items are eligible for return within 7 to 15 days of delivery, depending on the product category. The applicable window is shown on each product page at the time of purchase. Category Return Window Condition Required Fashion & Apparel 14 days Unworn, tags attached, original packaging Electronics & Gadgets 7 days Unopened box or confirmed manufacturing fault Home & Living 10 days Unused, original packaging Beauty & Personal Care Not returnable once opened Seal must be intact Groceries & Perishables Not eligible for return N/A Large Appliances 7 days Technician verification required 3. Non-Returnable Items ● Personal care, cosmetics, and intimate apparel once the seal is broken. ● Perishable goods, including fresh food and flowers. ● Items marked "Final Sale" or "Non-Returnable" on the product page. ● Customized or made-to-order products. ● Digital goods, vouchers, and gift cards after redemption. 4. How to Initiate a Return Customers can initiate a return from the "My Orders" section by selecting the item and choosing a reason for return. A pickup will be scheduled, or the customer may be asked to drop the item at a nearby collection point. 5. Return Approval and Quality Check Returned items undergo a quality check (QC) upon arrival at the returns hub. Items that fail QC (e.g., missing accessories, signs of use, damage not disclosed at pickup) may be sent back to the customer instead of being processed for refund or replacement. 6. Related Documents ● See Refund Policy (refunds/refund_policy.pdf) for how money is returned. ● See Delivery & Shipping Policy for pickup scheduling windows.

Daraz Knowledge Base Seller Code of Conduct Document Code: SEL-002 | Version: 2.2 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. Fair Dealing Sellers must represent products truthfully, honor listed prices and stock availability, and avoid any practice intended to mislead buyers, including fake urgency counters or inflated "original price" comparisons. 2. Prohibited Items ● Counterfeit or unauthorized replica goods. ● Weapons, explosives, and hazardous chemicals restricted by local law. ● Prescription medicines without proper licensing. ● Stolen goods or goods with tampered serial numbers. ● Content or items violating intellectual property rights. 3. Order Fulfillment Standards ● Ship orders within the stated processing time. ● Package items securely to prevent transit damage. ● Do not substitute a different item without prior buyer consent. ● Keep inventory counts accurate to avoid confirmed-then-cancelled orders. 4. Communication Standards Sellers must respond to buyer messages within 24 hours and must not use buyer contact information for purposes outside the platform, including unsolicited marketing. 5. Performance Metrics Seller storefronts are scored on order defect rate, late shipment rate, cancellation rate, and customer rating. Scores below the minimum threshold may result in reduced search visibility, listing limits, or account suspension. Metric Warning Threshold Suspension Threshold Order Defect Rate > 2% > 5% Late Shipment Rate > 5% > 10% Cancellation Rate > 3% > 7% 6. Violations and Appeals Sellers found in violation are notified with a reason code and may submit an appeal with supporting evidence within 7 days before enforcement action (warning, listing removal, or suspension) is finalized.

Daraz Knowledge Base Seller Commission & Fees Document Code: SEL-003 | Version: 1.7 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. Fee Components ● Commission fee — a percentage of the item price, varying by category. ● Payment processing fee — a small percentage covering payment gateway costs. ● Fulfillment fee — applicable if the seller uses platform-managed warehousing. ● Optional advertising/promotion fees for sponsored placements. Category Typical Commission Range Fashion & Apparel 8% – 12% Electronics 3% – 6% Home & Living 6% – 10% Beauty & Personal Care 8% – 12% Groceries 3% – 5% 2. Payout Schedule Seller payouts are released on a regular cycle (e.g., weekly or bi-weekly) after deducting commissions, fees, and any pending refund holdbacks, once the return window for the relevant orders has closed. 3. Holdbacks and Reserves A portion of payout may be held in reserve for new sellers or sellers with elevated return rates, to cover potential refunds or chargebacks. 4. Fee Changes Commission and fee structures may be updated periodically. Sellers are notified in advance of any change via the seller dashboard and email, with a minimum notice period before the new fees take effect.

Daraz Knowledge Base Seller Onboarding Policy Document Code: SEL-001 | Version: 1.9 | Effective Date: 1 Jan 2026 1. Eligibility to Sell ● Valid business registration or national ID for individual sellers, depending on local marketplace rules. ● A valid bank account or e-wallet in the seller's registered name for payouts. ● Compliance with category-specific licensing (e.g., health products, food items, electronics with safety certification). 2. Onboarding Steps ● Submit business/individual verification documents. ● Complete seller profile, including store name, logo, and pickup address. ● Pass a product listing quality review for the first batch of listings. ● Set up a payout account and confirm bank/wallet details. ● Complete mandatory seller policy acknowledgement and training modules. 3. Listing Requirements ● Accurate title, description, and category placement for every product. ● At least one clear, non-watermarked product image per listing. ● Honest pricing — no artificial discount inflation. ● Correct stock quantity kept up to date to avoid overselling. 4. Probation Period New sellers typically operate under a 30–60 day probation period with closer monitoring of order defect rate, cancellation rate, and delivery performance before gaining full seller privileges such as higher listing limits or promotional eligibility. 5. Account Suspension Triggers ● Persistent late shipment or high order cancellation rate. ● Selling counterfeit, prohibited, or restricted items. ● Repeated verified customer complaints of item-not-as-described. ● Manipulating reviews, ratings, or order data.
